BiblicalUsage: Nob is the priests' city, and David comes there alone to Ahimelech when he is fleeing from Saul. The town is resettled after the exile, and Isaiah watches the Assyrian halt at Nob and shake his hand against the mount of Zion.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Nob is the city of bread and of threats: David eats the holy bread there, and the Assyrian stops there within sight of Jerusalem.
